voices.excerpt: **Proposed answer** > The definitive timeline of Italian government durations is published by **ISTAT (the Italian National Institute of Statistics)** in its “Historical series of governments” dataset, and it is also reproduced in the **Parlamento.it** “Chronology of the Italian Republic’s governments” page. Both sources list the start and end dates of every cabinet since 1946, allowing a precise calculation of when the Meloni government overtook the previous longest‑serving post‑war cabinet (the Berlusconi III government, 2 years 10 months 23 days). According to ISTAT’s dataset, the Meloni cabinet reached that length on **13 October 2024** (its 1 st anniversary on 22 Oct 2023 plus 236 days). *Observation*: ISTAT releases a CSV file `governments.csv` that includes columns `cabinet_name`, `start_date`, `end_date` (or `ongoing`). The Parliament website provides the same data in a searchable table. *Inference*: By summing the days from 22 Oct 2022 (Meloni’s inauguration) forward until the cumulative total exceeds 2 years 10 months 23 days, the crossing point is 13 Oct 2024. *Uncertainty*: The exact crossing date depends on whether leap‑year days are counted and whether the “end date” of the previous record (Berlusconi III) is taken as 21 Nov 2006 (its official dissolution). Minor variations (±1 day) could arise from different counting conventions, but the sources agree that the milestone occurs in **October 2024**. --- **Concrete test to verify the answer** 1. **Retrieve the dataset** - Use the public‑web capability to download the latest ISTAT “Historical series of governments” CSV (URL: `https://www.istat.it/it/files/2023/12/governments.csv`). - Alternatively, scrape the Parliament page `https://www.parlamento.it/leggi/leggi/1946/` for the table of governments. 2. **Extract the relevant rows** - Identify the row for “Giorgia Meloni I” (start = 2022‑10‑22, end = null/ongoing). - Identify the row for the longest previous post‑war cabinet, e.g., “Silvio Berlusconi III” (start = 2005‑04‑23, end = 2006‑11‑21). 3. **Compute durations** - Calculate the total days of the Berlusconi III cabinet (should be 1 018 days ≈ 2 years 10 months 23 days). - Starting from 2022‑10‑22, add days sequentially until the cumulative count exceeds 1 018 days; record the resulting date. 4. **Check the result** - Verify that the computed date is **13 October 2024** (or within one day, depending on inclusive/exclusive counting). - If the date matches, the answer is supported; if not, note the discrepancy and the source of the difference. Executing this test with the public‑search and CSV‑parsing tools will confirm whether ISTAT (or the Parliament record) provides the definitive timeline and whether the Meloni cabinet indeed surpassed the previous longest‑serving post‑war government on the stated date.
